cards.title: Hour 14 produced an extreme error spike
cards.detail: Hour 14 had 1,460 errors out of 9,225 requests, an error rate of 15.8%, versus 31 errors out of 8,899 requests in a typical hour (0.35%). This hour contributed 67.3% of the week’s 2,169 errors and warrants investigation by time-based deployment, dependency, and capacity signals.

cards.title: Caller-07 has unusually high cost per request
cards.detail: Caller-07 spent $174.12 on 1,180 requests, or $0.148 per request, about 9.5 times caller-01’s $0.016 per request. Inspect its model or routing selection and its 4.0% cache hit rate before further volume growth.

cards.title: Traffic and spend are concentrated in caller-01
cards.detail: Caller-01 generated 105,832 requests, 51.6% of all traffic, and $1,643.86 of spend, 49.0% of the weekly total. Apply caller-specific quotas, monitoring, and capacity planning because changes there can materially affect the system.

cards.title: Ten callers have persistently low cache hit rates
cards.detail: Callers 03, 05, 07, 09, 11, 13, 15, 17, 21, and 23 account for 44,951 requests, 21.9% of total traffic, with cache hit rates from 4.0% to 8.9%; caller-01 achieves 87.0%. Review cache-key consistency, request normalization, and cache eligibility for this cohort.

cards.title: Model-alpha is the highest-latency major model
cards.detail: Model-alpha handled 86,080 requests and had a 2,454 ms p95 latency, the highest among models with substantial volume; model-gamma had 1,310 ms p95 on 36,892 requests. Evaluate routing or prompt changes for latency-sensitive traffic, while accounting for alpha’s $1,409.02 spend.
